previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, atrial fibrillation on warfarin, prior strokes, type II diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation presenting with shortness of breath, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema. He had significant fluid overload with a weight of 139.2 kg, up from prior discharge. The exacerbation was attributed to poor dietary salt intake and suboptimal diuretic use. He was started on IV furosemide and showed clinical improvement with fluid removal. However, he discontinued the IV diuretic and left the hospital against medical advice before reaching his dry weight. His INR was subtherapeutic at 1.9, increasing stroke risk, but he declined extended monitoring. Ophthalmology recommended switching from fluorometholone to a tapering course of prednisolone eye drops for chronic blepharoconjunctivitis. Podiatry assessed increased foot drainage and attributed it to fluid overload rather than infection. He was discharged on increased oral diuresis with torsemide 60 mg twice daily, with instructions for low-salt diet, daily weight monitoring, and close follow-up.
